perItemFindings.one_line: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=incremental below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The main completeness theorem establishes decidability through exhaustive DAG enumeration and generic real-closed-field quantifier elimination, but supplies no degree, height, certificate-length, or usable runtime bound, so it does not yet justify the proposed operational use in Tetrad or GSP. The sole worked cross-MEC example produces an ambiguity certificate rather than a common effect missed by existing graphical criteria, leaving the claimed law-restricted identification advantage without a substantive positive example. General separating tables are only real algebraic, while rational replacement and effective height control remain explicitly open. The inference theorem conditions on an externally fixed oracle and quotient class and is a routine finite-dimensional delta-method result, not an end-to-end discovery-and-inference guarantee. The delivered contribution is therefore a narrow exact-decidability framework rather than a field-level causal identification result. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

HALTED AT TRIAGE: the math panel returned `revise` and its findings were never repaired, so this note is NOT established as mathematically sound — do not bank it as downgraded on this verdict alone. Open findings: novelty-positioning@thm:sparse-simid-completeness, comparator-overclaim@prop:strict-beyond-teh
